explanation: A form can correctly refuse invalid input and preserve the saved value without using the reporter's preferred error phrase, extra message or additional red outline. This pattern matches those reviewed feedback preferences when valid corrections work and no applicable requirement for the requested treatment is established. Verify the actual rejection, recovery and saved state rather than judging only the wording. Proven silent refusal, misleading success, an applicable accessibility requirement or inability to recover is outside this narrow rejection.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, follow this workflow: Sign in as eval and open Releases > New Release in the seeded eval/harbor-handbook repository. Enter a fresh unique tag name, keep main as the target, and leave release title and body blank. Click Create Tag Only and confirm the tag-created message and the tag Code page. Return through Releases > New Release, enter the same tag and confirm the Existing tag helper. Click Create Tag Only again and observe the release-exists validation error on the form. The rejected report expected: After the first Create Tag Only action, the standalone tag should exist without a release. Retrying with that existing tag may be rejected as a duplicate tag, but should not claim a release exists when the tag-only flow did not create one. It claimed this outcome: The first Create Tag Only submission creates the tag and opens its Code page. Retrying the same action for that existing tag displays “A release with this tag name already exists.” The duplicate is rejected; no publishing failure or data loss was established. Review concluded: User-approved rejection of the wording-only complaint. The existing tag is correctly rejected as a duplicate in the shared New Release form. The user does not consider the shared release-exists wording an actionable bug for this eval; no functional failure is established.

explanation: A markup editor turns typed symbols into formatting, so the exact saved characters determine what should appear. This pattern matches a report of broken Markdown rendering when the editor source actually lacks the claimed emphasis markers, already contains an automatically inserted task prefix, or lacks a separator required by the syntax. Compare the saved source with the output instead of assuming the intended keystrokes were all retained. Recreating a similar example later does not prove the historical input was identical.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, follow this workflow: Sign in as eval and open New Release in eval/harbor-handbook without publishing a release. Compare the earlier and later Preview attempts in the original recording: the earlier editor value is plain Bold phrase, with no Markdown emphasis markers. After the retry, the editor value contains a Markdown heading followed by **Bold phrase**. Open Preview and inspect the correctly formatted phrase. Keep the distinction between the two inputs: plain text should preview as plain text, while the corrected Markdown should preview as bold. The rejected report expected: Text formatted with the Bold toolbar should appear visibly bold in the release-notes Preview. It claimed this outcome: The Write view visibly contained `# Lifecycle Deep Bold Preview` and `**Bold phrase**`; Preview rendered the heading as a heading but displayed “Bold phrase” in regular weight, still unchanged after six seconds. Review concluded: User-approved rejection after reviewing the earlier and later Preview states. The earlier attempt replaced the toolbar’s Markdown markers and submitted plain text. The corrected retry preserved **Bold phrase**, rendered a strong element at semibold weight, and the user confirmed that the later Preview visibly showed bold. The observed change follows the changed input; no Preview failure is established.

explanation: In a code-hosting application, a release announcement and the version tag it describes are related but separate objects. Deleting the release while choosing to retain the tag can leave its title or notes attached to that surviving tag without keeping the release published. This pattern matches a report that calls those retained tag details an undeleted release. Verify which object was deleted and which one was explicitly retained before treating surviving data as a deletion failure.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, follow this workflow: Publish a release on a tag without ticking the tag-message option. Delete the release with Delete Release (not Delete Tag). Open the tag's page, the repository tags.rss feed, and New Release for that tag. The rejected report expected: The reported expectation is that deleting a release removes its title and notes from Gitea while keeping the Git tag. It claimed this outcome: After deleting a published release on a tag without its own message, /releases/tag/<tag> still showed the release title and notes, tags.rss still carried the notes, and New Release for the tag pre-filled them. The release was gone from the Releases list. Review concluded: User-rejected after source review. Delete Release keeps the tag row and only marks it as a tag, so the title and notes it carried stay attached to the tag. The reviewer judged keeping that text on the surviving tag to be acceptable, consistent with tags being expected to show their message, rather than a defect.

explanation: An interface can display an edit or newly created item before its background save, multi-step creation or notification processing has finished. This pattern matches reports that interrupt that unfinished work with a hard refresh, immediately run the previously saved configuration or check results before processing completes, then call the old state loss of a completed operation. Verify the actual completion and reread the same item or recipient. Acknowledged-save loss, ordinary navigation discarding valid edits, or an effect still absent after completion needs separate evidence.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, follow this workflow: Open a New Release form at 768×900. Enter text in the notes, select it and click the Bold toolbar button. Click Preview. The rejected report expected: The reporter expects Preview to show the newly entered notes in bold. It claimed this outcome: After entering 'Responsive toolbar note', selecting it, clicking Bold and then Preview at 768×900, the Preview pane was reported to still show the earlier preview. Review concluded: Not reproduced. Preview sends the current notes on every click and replaces the pane with the server's response (web_src/js/features/comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts), which rendered the text as <strong> each time. The previous preview stays visible only until that response arrives (about 50–100 ms), a loading state rather than stale content. Bold rendering itself is already rejected as gitea-pass2-014.
